scenarios.expected: Recognized archives expose the specified ordered names, metadata, diagnostics, and decoded bytes.
Embedded names remain bounded, independently represented, and semantically identical after round trip.
Malformed structures are rejected or classified as the specified tolerated noncanonical disposition without unbounded reads.
Unsupported compressed payload encodings fail with a stable unsupported or format outcome before unsafe consumption.
Unsupported encode codecs are rejected before opening sources or publishing destination artifacts.
Stored and mixed-compression inputs encode canonically and decode to the original ordered entries.
Unsafe or colliding entry names are rejected before destination effects and cannot escape the extraction root.
Stored entries encode canonically and decode to the original ordered names and bytes.
Zlib entries round trip through the independent wire validator with exact decoded content.
LZ4-frame entries use the qualified profile and round trip with exact decoded content.
JBSA and the digest-pinned Conformance Oracle cross-decode equivalent semantic content in both applicable directions.
BSA 0x69 uses 24-byte folder records and diagnoses nonzero padding without losing inspectability.
BSA 0x69 automatic, explicit Xbox, and cleared miscellaneous flags match the specified profile behavior.
BSA 0x69 sharing, splitting, and logical ordering publish readable deterministic archive parts.
The thin CLI selects BSA 0x69 explicitly and rejects incompatible codec and family combinations.
LZ4-frame processing remains within admitted heap, native, scratch, and output bounds.
Cancellation is observed before publication and all LZ4 credits and owned resources are released.
Focused Archive Family checkpoints record throughput, memory observations, and derived output size under bound conditions.
Family-specific naming, hashing, flags, compression boundaries, source overlays, sharing, splitting, determinism, and empty or multi-entry interactions match their owning specifications.
Starfield v3 method-3 entries use the qualified level-12 raw-LZ4 profile and round trip exact ordered bytes.
Starfield General emits the canonical extra header and selects v2 without a method or v3 with method 3 solely from the compressed codec.
The thin CLI maps -sf1 stored and zlib to v2 and raw LZ4 to v3 method 3, then cross-decodes the output.
An independent bounded scanner accepts canonical Starfield v2 zlib and v3 raw-LZ4 while requiring exact complete payload consumption.
Bounded stored DDS chunks remain diagnosed noncanonical and mixed stored/compressed chunks reconstruct in serialized order.
One through four independently framed DDS chunks retain contiguous mip ranges and reconstruct canonical envelopes with opaque payload bytes in serialized order.
An independent bounded scanner validates Starfield DDS v2 zlib and v3 method-3 raw-LZ4 chunk headers, payload consumption, and reconstructed DDS bytes.
Microsoft DirectXTex built from the recorded source revision accepts every independently generated PC DDS after Starfield v2 zlib and v3 method-3 raw-LZ4 reconstruction.
The thin CLI selects Starfield DDS v2 zlib or v3 method-3 raw-LZ4, rejects stored DDS encoding, and cross-decodes the result.
DDS chunk decoding and reconstruction admit packed, decoded, entry, native, and output bounds before allocation or publication effects.
Raw-LZ4 native capability, size admission, memory credits, invalid input, and stable failure mapping are checked before output effects.
Raw-LZ4 cancellation and callback failures release credits without publishing destination effects.

Without an explicit profile the CLI rejects malformed selectors and switches before source effects, reports failures on stderr, and requires explicit replacement while preserving pack, inspect, dump, and unpack results.

Only explicit bsarch-1.0/v1 selection activates the complete immutable CLI deviation bundle, including parsing, family priority, source omission, stdout placement, information status, and replacement, without bypassing source safety.

The immutable profile uses the actual Windows ANSI code page or fails closed without native access, confines Starfield v3 zlib fallback to profiled bounded decode, and never enables prohibited stored DDS encoding; deferred Xbox inference makes no first-release claim.
One and multiple workers preserve archive bytes, ordered CLI and library observations, diagnostics, progress, split and sharing choices, and extracted content across the eight writable families.

The Ctrl+C callback requests idempotent cooperative cancellation; cancellation and worker or publication failure settle admitted work, bound resources and failure ordering, restore predecessors when required, and leave no unpublished destination effects.
Semantic progress remains ordered while redirected stderr and --no-progress suppress only presentation, preserving successful CLI records and archive bytes.
CLI warnings and failures retain stable identifiers, prescribed streams and exit statuses while operation failures preserve primary ordering and exact residual artifacts.
Fallout 4 v1 General and DDS readers distinguish tolerated metadata warnings from malformed records, corrupt payloads, and resource-limit failures before destination effects.
Unsafe General and DDS entry names are inspectable but cannot escape the extraction root or alter the destination before preflight rejects them.

General v1 stored, zlib, mixed, zero-length, name-table and split records and DDS v1 stored or mixed chunks, PC mip boundaries, formats, cubemaps, sharing, and reconstruction retain content and deterministic output across worker counts.
Fallout 4 General and DDS v1 selectors, implicit DDS zlib compression, information, pack, and unpack are carried through the thin CLI using public requests and reports.
Fallout 4 DDS v1 PC encoding rejects an Xbox input envelope before destination publication; deferred Xbox encoding is not counted as supported.

The digest-pinned local Oracle and JBSA cross-decode Fallout 4 General and DDS v1 in both directions with independently validated candidate wire and exact source content; Oracle-only zero padding is classified explicitly.
Fallout 4 v7/v8 General and DDS archives retain their exact wire version, v1-shaped records, ordered names and hashes, zlib framing, and decoded bytes; v7 General remains synthetic-only.
Every Fallout 4 v7/v8 General or DDS encode request fails as unsupported before source factories or destination artifacts are touched.
The thin CLI automatically detects, dumps, and unpacks every Fallout 4 v7/v8 General and DDS selector without exposing an encode selector.
Truncated records, invalid spans, and corrupt complete zlib streams are rejected without unbounded reads.
Payloads framed as raw DEFLATE, raw LZ4, or LZ4 frame data are rejected when v7/v8 records require stored bytes or complete zlib streams.
Entry, metadata, decoded-byte, and reconstruction limits reject v7/v8 inputs before excess allocation or destination effects.
Independent bounded scanners validate each v7/v8 envelope, record, name/hash, zlib frame, payload extent, DDS mip range, and reconstructed opaque bytes.
The digest-pinned Conformance Oracle decodes the same project-authored v7/v8 bytes; this is decode-only and does not establish a v7 General producer.
Stored/zlib selection, physical order, names and hashes, exact sharing, random entry opens, and safe extraction retain the shared BA2 behavior under v7/v8 selectors.
Version 7 and 8 DDS chunks reconstruct canonical PC DDS headers and exact independently validated opaque mip bytes.
Read-only local samples corroborate Creation Kit v8 General and shipping v7/v8 DDS decoding without committing proprietary bytes; v7 General is intentionally excluded.
Absolute, traversal, and Windows-invalid names remain inspectable but make v7/v8 extraction ineligible before destination effects.
Local decode-only checkpoints cover metadata, unpack or DDS reconstruction, random entry opens, and heap-pool peaks without timing prohibited encoding.
